comment: Catalogue of the fabric icons used in the A+ icon row (sheet column K, 'Fabric Icons'). Two populations exist in the Figma file and they are NOT the same set. 'bank' = the ICON BANK the user built on Page 2 (a 19px reference catalogue, each icon labelled '<Name>: <description>'). 'production' = the full-size icons (150.86px ring, 40.23px label) that live inside the real A+ designs on the same page and are what the plugin actually clones today. Names present in one population and not the other are listed under coverage. Figma imageHash values only resolve inside this one file, so the artwork is also exported to the .svg / .png files beside this index as the durable backup.

ring.comment: The circle behind each glyph. The two populations style it differently; the renderer must use the production ring when it builds an icon from bank artwork.

bank.note: Two bank ellipses (1105:2041 on Ribbed Texture, 1105:2127 on High Lycra) stroke #5E5E5E instead of #5C5C5C.

ring.scaleFactorNote: 150.86 / 18.820038 = 8.016. A bank icon is an exact 8x reduction of production scale, so bank artwork can be scaled up to production size without redrawing it.

label.comment: Typography of the label under a production icon. Bank labels are not usable as-is: they read '<Name>: <description>' and must be split on the first colon.
label.colorNote: Some older production icons use pure #FFFFFF; both read as white on the fabric card.

aliases.comment: Sheet spelling -> canonical icon name. Keys are already normalised (lowercased, every run of non-alphanumeric characters collapsed to a single space, trimmed), which is the same normalisation buildIconIndex applies to both sides before it compares them. That normalisation alone already resolves case and hyphen/space variants ('Sweat Wicking' == 'sweat-wicking' == 'SWEAT–WICKING'), so this map only needs to carry genuine renamings. Every entry here is either taken from an instruction written inside the bank or is a morphological variant of a single unambiguous bank name; nothing here is a guess between two candidate icons.

buttery soft.quote: Super-Soft, buttery soft, lightweight - have same feather icon

super soft.note: Redundant with normalisation, kept explicit because it is the spelling the live sheet actually uses (Training and Athleisure-Lifestyle rows write 'Super Soft').

bio washed.note: The live sheet writes 'Bio-Washed'. The bank has exactly one bio-wash icon, so this is a morphological variant, not a choice between candidates.

deliberatelyNotAliased.comment: Sheet values that look close to a bank name but map to more than one candidate. Aliasing these would silently ship the wrong glyph to Amazon, so they are left unresolved and reported instead. A human decision is needed before any of these can be added above.

stretchy.note: Resolves exactly against the production icon 'Stretchy', so it needs no alias. It is listed here only to record that it must NOT be aliased to 'Super Stretch', 'Multi Stretch' or 'High Lycra' — the bank offers three stretch icons and nothing says which one 'Stretchy' means.

ultra lightweight.note: 'Ultra-Lightweight' is a distinct claim from 'Lightweight' and has no icon of its own in either population.

backup.comment: Why these files exist: a Figma imageHash is meaningless outside file DyUWRDA1JPo75nWMj5UoJe, so the exported bytes are the only copy of this artwork that survives the file being lost, forked or cleaned up.
backup.exportedFrom: the glyph node of each icon (not the whole icon group), so the long '<Name>: <description>' bank label is not baked into the artwork
backup.svgNote: Every .svg parses as XML and is self-contained: a raster glyph is embedded as a base64 data URI inside the SVG, so the .svg alone is a complete backup. The matching .png is the same artwork as the original uploaded bitmap, kept because it is smaller and easier to re-import.
backup.vectorOnlyNote: These four glyphs are true vectors, so there is no .png — the .svg is the artwork itself, not a wrapper.
backup.rasterNote: Every other glyph is a raster image fill, not vector line art. The .svg is therefore a bitmap wrapped in SVG and will not scale cleanly beyond its native pixel size.

notExported.why: it is a plain circle, identical across every icon, and is fully specified under 'ring' above — exporting 16 copies of the same circle would add nothing

notExported.what: a separate SVG for each duplicate bank entry
notExported.why: the duplicates are byte-identical to the entry already exported; the duplicate node ids are recorded under each icon's 'duplicateOf'
